origin.usage: rollsum(x, k, fill = if (na.pad) NA, na.pad = FALSE, align = c("center", "left", "right"), ...)

arguments.name: k
arguments.text: Window width in observations. It is truncated toward zero.

arguments.name: fill
arguments.text: Three fill values for the left side, the interior gaps, and the right side. A shorter vector is recycled and a longer one keeps the first three. NULL drops those positions. "extend" repeats an end and linearly interpolates an interior gap.

arguments.name: align
arguments.text: Where the window sits on its result time: center, left, or right. A unique prefix is enough. NULL selects center.
Further arguments. A missing value in rollmean, rollsum, or rollmedian is handled by rollapply, and those arguments are passed through.

origin.details: The fast path keeps a running sum. Integer input stays integer when every window is full and fill does not force a double. A missing value, or a width longer than the series, uses rollapply. An empty series is returned unchanged. rollsumr is the right-aligned wrapper.
origin.value: An object of the same kind as x with the rolling sum. A plain vector returns the values.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Series, vector, or matrix. A Zoo keeps its index.

arguments.name: k
arguments.text: Window width in observations. It is truncated toward zero. This is k in R.

arguments.name: fill
arguments.text: Three fill values for the left side, the interior gaps, and the right side. A shorter vector is recycled and a longer one keeps the first three. NULL drops those positions. "extend" repeats an end and linearly interpolates an interior gap.

arguments.name: na_pad
arguments.text: Deprecated. True fills with NA. This is na.pad in R.
